title: Noninvasive and Invasive Renal Hypoxia Monitoring in a Porcine Model of Hemorrhagic Shock
protocol: Cut a 6 cm piece of 3/8 in thermoplastic elastomer tubing.
Cut 25 mm pieces of both 1/8 in and 3/16 in PVC tubing.
Cut 31 mm pieces of both 1/8 in and 3/16 in PVC tubing.
Drill a hole in the top of the non-vented cap to fit the exposed tip of the temperature probe, starting with a 3/32 in drill bit and then using a 1/8 in drill bit.
Use a 5/32 in drill bit to drill out the top part of the T-connector to fit the oxygen sensor.
Slide the shorter piece of the 1/8 in PVC tubing over the inlet side of the flow sensor.
Slide the longer 1/8 in piece of PVC tubing over the outlet side of the flow sensor.
Slide the shorter and longer 3/16 in pieces of PVC tubing over the corresponding lengths of the 1/8 in PVC tubing.
Insert the barbed end of the male luer lock connector into the open end of the 1/8 in PVC tubing.
Mix the biocompatible glue.
Expose the tip of the temperature probe by removing any protective sheathing or tubing.
Fill the inside of the tubing of the thermistor with biocompatible glue but do not cover the exposed tip.
Assemble the parts as shown.
Use the glue to secure each luer lock connection.
Insert the thermistor in the non-vented cap.
Secure prior to sliding the 3/8 in TPE tubing over the barbed end.
Sedate the animal with a combined intramuscular injection of Ketamine (2.2 mg/kg), Xylazine (2.2 mg/kg), and Telazol (4.4 mg/kg).
Place an appropriately sized cuffed endotracheal tube with the assistance of a laryngoscope.
Apply eye lubricant to both eyes.
Mechanically ventilate the animal with 1.5%-3.0% gaseous isoflurane mixed in oxygen.
Set the fraction of inspired oxygen between 40%-100%.
Set the positive end-expiratory pressure to 4 cm H2O.
Set the tidal volume to 6-8 mL/kg.
Adjust the respiratory rate and tidal volume to maintain end-tidal CO2 of 35-45 mmHg.
Monitor jaw tone and palpebral reflex approximately every 15 minutes during the experiment.
Assess absence of spontaneous movement throughout the experiment.
Monitor mucous membrane color as an indicator of tissue perfusion.
Evaluate capillary refill time to assess tissue perfusion.
Measure heart rate regularly during the experiment.
Use pulse oximetry to monitor oxygen saturation and pulse rate.
Monitor end-tidal CO2 levels continuously.
Maintain core body temperature using a warming blanket.
Record electrocardiogram readings throughout the procedure.
Position the animal in dorsal recumbency on the table.
Secure each leg of the animal to the operating table.
Prepare all puncture sites by scrubbing with chlorhexidine and alcohol three times alternately.
Allow the final chlorhexidine application to dry completely.
Drape the surgical site in a sterile manner after preparing the skin.
Infiltrate all puncture and incision sites locally with 2% lidocaine for pain relief.
Place a 9 Fr catheter in the right external jugular vein using ultrasound guidance and Seldinger technique.
Insert a 7 Fr catheter into the right femoral vein under ultrasound guidance for resuscitation purposes.
Introduce a 7 Fr sheath into the right brachial artery with ultrasound guidance.
Position a 7 Fr sheath in the right femoral artery using ultrasound guidance.
Place a 7 Fr sheath in the left femoral artery under ultrasound guidance.
Place a 5 Fr sheath in the right or left carotid artery under ultrasound guidance.
Monitor pressure distal to the balloon of the resuscitative endovascular occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) catheter via the left femoral artery sheath.
Connect a disposable pressure transducer to the arterial catheter that is distal to the REBOA balloon.
Monitor pressure proximal to the balloon of the REBOA catheter via the carotid artery sheath.
Connect a disposable pressure transducer to the arterial catheter that is proximal to the REBOA balloon.
Make an incision along the midline of the abdomen, starting at the inferior part of the sternum and ending at the pubis for a midline laparotomy.
Identify the bladder within the opened abdomen.
Perform a cystotomy by making a small incision in the bladder.
Insert the tip of a 20 Fr urinary catheter into the bladder through the cystotomy.
Close the cystotomy around the urinary catheter using a purse string suture.
Secure the urinary catheter to the skin with sutures after ensuring it is in place.
Prior to connecting the outlet of the catheter to the urine collection bag, insert the cone-shaped end of the noninvasive PuO2 monitor into the catheter outlet.
Place the open tubing at the end of the novel PuO2 monitor over the cone-shaped connector on the tubing connected to the urine collection bag.
Remove the spleen to eliminate hemorrhage-induced auto-transfusion.
Locate the spleen.
Identify the hilum of the spleen or the site where the splenic artery and vein enter the spleen.
Clamp and transect each vessel.
Ligate each vessel using modified Miller knots using 2-0 sutures.
Place the instrument to measure bladder PuO2 and tissue oxygenation.
Measure PuO2 at the outlet of the bladder.
Identify the balloon on the catheter.
Just below the balloon, make an incision along the long axis of the catheter without cutting the lumen that connects to the balloon.
Insert a t-connector containing the sensing material into the incision.
Use tissue glue to secure the t-connector in place.
Connect the fiber optic cable from the bladder data collection device to the connector that contains the sensing material.
Create a new file on the data collection device and note the time difference between the stand-alone collection device and other devices used in the experiment.
Push the back arrow to reach the main menu.
Go to measurement settings and click Ok.
Use the arrows to highlight the measurement browser box and push Ok.
Push the right arrow to create a new file.
Type in the name of the new file and select Done.
Highlight the new file name and select Ok.
Navigate to the measurement screen and click on Ok to start recording.
Measure medullary renal tissue oxygenation.
Identify the location of the kidney internally.
Move the bowel to have a clear line of sight and access to the entire kidney.
Insert the sensor into an 18 gauge catheter.
Adjust the luer lock connector on the sensor so that the tip is exposed.
Remove the catheter, place it over an 18 gauge needle, and insert both the needle and catheter into the renal medulla under ultrasound guidance.
Remove the needle while keeping the catheter in place.
Thread the tissue sensor through the catheter and connect it to the catheter using the luer lock.
Secure the catheter with tissue glue.
Connect the tissue sensor to the data collection box.
Wait for 10 minutes before beginning the experimental protocol, considering this period as a baseline.
Ensure that the mean arterial pressure (MAP) is ≥65 mmHg prior to starting the procedure.
Give up to two 5 mL/kg boluses of isotonic crystalloid solution if MAP is below 65 mmHg.
Infuse norepinephrine at 0.02 µg/kg/min until target MAP is achieved, if necessary.
Remove 25% (estimated as 60 mL/kg) of the animal's blood volume through the right brachial artery sheath over 1 hour into a citrated blood collection bag kept in a warm water bath at 37 °C.
Perform randomization to assign animals to either the REBOA with whole blood or REBOA with crystalloids group (n = 6 for each group).
Insert a 7 Fr REBOA catheter in the right femoral artery sheath.
Place the balloon of the catheter immediately superior to the diaphragm and confirm its location using fluoroscopy.
Inflate the REBOA balloon at t = 30 min to occlude the aorta for 45 min.
Transfuse each animal with their shed blood over 15 min starting at t = 70 min.
Infuse intravenous calcium over 10 min to prevent citrate-induced hypocalcemia.
Deflate the REBOA balloon over 10 min starting at t = 75 min.
Resuscitate the animal with fluids and norepinephrine until t = 360 min to maintain a MAP > 65 mmHg.
Collect any remaining blood or urine samples.
Euthanize the animal by injecting a combination of Pentobarbital Sodium (390 mg) and Phenytoin Sodium (50 mg) at 1 mL/10 lbs.
Discard data associated with High Flow Rate error.
Discard data associated with Air-in-Line error.
Track volume that flows past the sensor in the backward direction when flow becomes negative.
After flow becomes positive again, track the volume.
Compare positive flow volume to the previously recorded negative flow volume.
Include only measurements from recently voided urine after comparing volumes.
